answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents join the network by committing stake to a registry anchored like an anchored reef of trust. Each identity anchors cryptographic attestation chains verifying provenance, validated privately using zero-knowledge proofs. To prevent fake swarms from spoofing diverse entities—distinguished by tags like saffron and juniper—the staking protocol mandates exponential capital exhaustion for each incremental identity spawned by an operator, imposing superlinear attacker cost O(2^n).
